scope: Brookwood Labor College first custody pass: Josephine Kaczor, Nazareth hosiery organizer; existing records preserved.

newleader1930.label: The New Leader, March 15, 1930, page 3, Nazareth, Pa. Strikers Keep Fight Strong. Names Josephine Kaczor, Brookwood graduate, among eleven acquitted riot defendants assessed costs ($150 for Kaczor). Reports their refusal to pay, jail, immediate hunger strike and release four days later. Original column visually checked; publication date is not a custody endpoint.

portrait.label: Labor Age, February 1930, printed page 25 (PDF page 32), Return to the Picket Line. Original caption explicitly identifies Josephine Kaczor as fourth from the right. Describes an overnight Northampton County detention, not the separate four-day hunger-strike episode. Photographer uncredited. Exact pixel crop from the embedded scan.

brookwood_archive.label: Walter P. Reuther Library, Guide to the Brookwood Labor College Photographs, LAV000567_BLC. Catalog identifies Josephine Kaczor in a student group photograph. Archive lead corroborating Brookwood association; that different photograph is not the assigned portrait.

prisoner.name: Josephine Kaczor
prisoner.description: Josephine Kaczor was a labor organizer and Brookwood Labor College graduate involved in the 1929–1930 hosiery strike in Nazareth, Pennsylvania, against contracts barring union membership. A March 1930 report named her among eleven defendants acquitted of rioting but still assessed court costs; her share was $150. The strikers refused payment, were jailed, and won release after four days on hunger strike. Contemporary coverage also records repeated strike arrests. The dates of her four-day confinement and her birth and death dates remain unverified.

cases.charges: Rioting allegation during the Nazareth hosiery strike; detention for refusing court costs after acquittal
cases.convicted: Acquitted of rioting; assessed $150 in court costs despite the acquittal
cases.sentence: Four days of actual jail confinement after refusing court costs, followed by release after a hunger strike, as reported March 15, 1930. This was not a four-day sentence for a riot conviction. Exact custody dates and the specific facility for this episode remain unverified.

Actual multi-day confinement is explicit; it is not inferred from a sentence. Dates of commitment and physical release are unverified.
